articles.byline: BY PERRY SMITH, HOMETOWNSTATION.COM | WEDNESDAY, NOV 19, 2014
articles.text: [KHTS] – Saugus Union School District officials named Chris Trunkey as the newest member of their governing board Tuesday, filling a seat left vacant by Doug Bryce’s departure in September. Trunkey, a film executive who was narrowly defeated by Bryce in last November’s school board election, was sworn in at 7:30 p.m. during the regularly scheduled board meeting. File photo: Trunkey participates in a candidate forum in October 2013. “I feel very comfortable working with (Trunkey),” said board member Judy Umeck, after the selection. “He has a constituency here and I look forward to the new and fresh ideas he has shared.” Trunkey and Bruce Fox, a member of the Glendale Police Department and former Castaic School Board member, were the final two choices after each of the four candidates were interviewed by the board for 20 minutes. Trunkey is on the site council for West Creek Academy, a Saugus Union elementary school in Valencia. He was chosen over Fox, Julie Coate and Mathew Ferguson. Trunkey lost to Bryce by 49 votes last November. Bryce stepped down at the end of September in order to pursue a job opportunity in San Diego. He left his job at Crane Aerospace for a job at Honeywell, where he’ll be working with “process improvement activities and quality improvement activities.” Trunkey is the board’s second appointment. David Powell was chosen by the board to replace Stephen Winkler in July. Trunkey is CFO for Phoenix Pictures, a production company “led by Mike Medavoy and Arnie Messer, two of the industry’s most respected senior executives,” according to the company’s website. “Phoenix has established a reputation for consistently developing first-rate projects with some of Hollywood’s top creative talent.”

articles.byline: BY PERRY SMITH, HOMETOWNSTATION.COM | TUESDAY, NOV 11, 2014
articles.text: [KHTS] – Four potential candidates applied to fill the vacancy of the Saugus Union School District governing board, officials said Tuesday. Bruce Fox, Julie C. Coate, Mathew Clarke Ferguson and Christopher Trunkey applied for the vacancy created after former board member Doug Bryce announced his plans to resign and move to San Diego for a job opportunity. “We’re definitely looking forward to being a complete board again,” said board President Paul De La Cerda. The candidates will be publicly interviewed at a special meeting to be formally announced by the district Wednesday, he said, which will take place Nov. 18 before a regularly scheduled board meeting. The appointment will be the district’s second in the last six months. After the courts approved vacating Stephen Winkler’s seat over the summer, officials names David Powell to the board in July. An investigation by district officials resulted in charges he maintained his residence outside district boundaries. SUSD officials are in the process of vetting applicants to ensure they meet the criteria, such as being over the age of 18, an eligible voter and a resident of the school district. After a candidate is selected by the board, they’ll be sworn in and take part of their first meeting that same evening, De La Cerda said. The state’s Education Code dictates how long the district has to fill the seat, he said, which was part of the reason why the swearing in is scheduled for the same evening. “Moving forward, we have a lot of work ahead of us, including the implementation of Measure EE, and our budget are two important areas that are coming up,” he said. More than 55 percent of voters approved the $148 million school-improvement bond measure last Tuesday to enhance facilities district-wide. “We’re very appreciative of our community supporting public education,” De La Cerda said. “We’re indebted to all of our volunteers who put in a lot of time and their own personal investments to help us.” The selection process is expected to be similar to the last appointment process as far as the structure, he added, but it could be a little different because there are fewer applicants. The format would be discussed and explained at the start of the meeting, he added.

The Hart School District Governing Board is seeking applications to fill three vacancies on the Citizen’s Oversight Committee formed to review expenditures of Measure V school bond funds. One member should be a senior citizen, others will be members at large. The committee meets monthly to review the district’s building plans and assure that Measure V funds are spent in accordance with the measure approved by local voters in 2001 for $158 million. Committee members appointed to fill the current vacancies will serve a two-year term or until all funds have been committed and expended. Applications are available online, along with guidelines at http://hartdistrict.org/oversight/MeasureV, click on Membership, then Application or Guidelines and download the forms. Applications are also available at the District Office located at 21515 Centre Pointe Pkwy, Santa Clarita, CA 91350. Completed applications are to be submitted to Pam Mencuri, William S. Hart Union High School District, 21515 Centre Pointe Parkway, Santa Clarita, CA, 91350 or emailed to [email protected] . Deadline for application submission is 4 p.m. Wednesday, November 7, 2012. Completed applications become public records and cannot be kept confidential by law. Contact Pam Mencuri at 661.753.5740 ext. 275 with any questions.
